subject.title: Discord DMs: inbound messages silently dropped (outbound works)

question: Should Discord account-scoped `allowFrom` keep narrowing/replacing the root allowlist for inbound DMs, or should root and account `allowFrom` be unioned for DM admission?
rationale: The direct repair for the reported root/account mismatch broadens who may start Discord DM agent sessions on narrowed accounts, so source inspection alone should not choose the security contract.

options.title: Preserve Account Narrowing
options.body: Keep account-scoped `allowFrom` as the default narrowing boundary and address this issue through explicit account configuration, diagnostics, and live validation of the multi-account DM path.

options.title: Union Root And Account Lists
options.body: Allow root-listed users through account DMs too, which may address the suspected root cause but broadens access for accounts that were intentionally narrowed.

options.title: Add Explicit Inheritance Policy
options.body: Introduce a documented opt-in inheritance mode only if maintainers want both root convenience and account-specific narrowing.

recommendation.title: Preserve Account Narrowing
recommendation.body: Keep account-scoped `allowFrom` as the default narrowing boundary and address this issue through explicit account configuration, diagnostics, and live validation of the multi-account DM path.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses Discord account config, shared DM access helpers, and sender-admission security semantics where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
